newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-GKN move on ruling stems share slide.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-GKN move on ruling stems share slide.

text.p: British engineering giant GKN Plc on Friday stopped a slide in its shares by swiftly announcing it would appeal against a U.S. court order to pay $600 million in damages for misusing advertising fees.

GKN said it expected to take its case to the U.S. court of appeals in a month or so to appeal against what has been described as one of the biggest awards against a British company in the United States, which was made on Thursday.
"We have been apprised by our lawyers and we think we are on strong grounds," a GKN spokesman told Reuters.
The award includes $591 million in punitive damages and $10 million in interests.
Before the market opened, traders had predicted the company's stock would plunge but after touching a low of 950 pence, it recovered to 1003 by 1345 GMT.
Analysts said GKN's quick reaction cleared up any uncertainties the market may have had.

"The market was over-discounting the worst case scenario," said Andy Chambers, industry analyst at SocGen. "We now have a clear figure of the provision and likely cash outflow from the litigation and we can ascertain what the real impact on earnings is likely to be."

Another City analyst said the amount of damages was above expectations but was confident it would be scaled down after an appeal. "It will definitely be lower, but what is important is it that now we see some direction," she said.

The U.S. district court's judgement ended four years of litigation involving Meineke Discount Mufflers, GKN's U.S. exhaust retailer which has been accused of improperly taking millions of dollars for its own use from an advertising fund built up by franchisees.
The jury found last month after a six-week trial that Meineke had committed fraud by taking the money in breach of contracts with franchisees.
GKN frustrated most analysts on Thursday by avoiding making any provisions for damages when it announced its 1996 accounts.

"We did not because we were not sure how much we should be providing. A range of figures were being speculated," the GKN spokesman said. The group had expressed fears last month that the damages could top $740 million. GKN has cash reserves of 528 million pounds.
The engineering group amended its account overnight by making a provision of 270 million pounds as exceptional charges. Its amended pretax, pre exceptional profits now stands at 92.8 million pounds.

"This includes interest and legal costs likely to accrue pending the outcome of the appeal and will be treated as an exceptional charge in the 1996 accounts," GKN said. The company's appeal is expected to take about 18 months to resolve.

U.S. district court judge Robert D. Potter tripled the jury's December 18 finding on compensatory damages which was put at $197 million. The original decision also had awarded another $150 million in punitive damages, now folded into the judge's award of $600.97 million.
Legal officials in the United States said the judgement would have far-reaching implications for franchisees and dealerships across the country.
